response.sql: SELECT ID, AVG(UA) AS avg_UA, AVG(HCT) AS avg_HCT FROM Laboratory GROUP BY ID HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN RA = '-' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 0 ORDER BY (AVG(HCT) IS NULL), AVG(HCT) DESC LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: Only patients with at least one Laboratory record are considered. Patients with no lab rows are excluded, since they have no averages to report. A lab record with a NULL RA is not treated as '-', so it does not disqualify the patient.
Ties in average hematocrit are broken arbitrarily, because the request gives no tie-break rule.

alternatives.interpretation: Patients with no laboratory records at all also count as having no '-' RA result. They would appear with NULL averages, after all patients who have hematocrit values.
alternatives.sql: SELECT p.ID, AVG(l.UA) AS avg_UA, AVG(l.HCT) AS avg_HCT FROM Patient p LEFT JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID = p.ID GROUP BY p.ID HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN l.RA = '-' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 0 ORDER BY (AVG(l.HCT) IS NULL), AVG(l.HCT) DESC LIMIT 10
